title: Introduce adaptive helper stack and compact tooltip patterns
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As the product grows, we have multiple competing approaches for showing field-level helper content: single-line helper text, inline error stacks, character counts, and small triggerable tooltips. These combinations behave inconsistently across dense and regular form densities, resulting in layout jumps, clipped helpers in constrained panels, and unclear a11y semantics.

Goal: Define a single adaptive helper-stack pattern plus a compact tooltip variant for advanced/optional guidance that: (1) preserves baseline alignment across density modes, (2) prevents layout shift when messages appear/disappear, (3) exposes clear accessibility semantics for screen readers, and (4) maps cleanly to our token system (spacing, typography, color, motion).

Deliverables:
- Visual spec for the adaptive helper stack (primary helper line + secondary metadata row) with spacing and token references for regular and compact densities.
- Interaction spec for the compact tooltip (trigger affordance, keyboard flow, dismiss behavior, viewport clipping strategy).
- Accessibility plan (aria attributes for announcements, focus management, and offscreen DOM for voiceover).
- Implementation notes for CSS variables and classes to ensure parity between React components and legacy vanilla inputs.
- QA checklist and unit/UI test cases (rendering under constraint widths, localization with long helpers, RTL).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Helper stack supports three states without layout shift: none -> helper -> helper+meta (meta = charcount/timeout) by reserving the vertical space for the two-line stack in both densities.
2) Compact tooltip behavior is optional per-field via prop and uses an accessible button with aria-expanded/aria-controls; tooltip content is not required to reserve vertical space.
3) Tokens documented: helper-font-size / helper-line-height / helper-gap / helper-color {regular, compact}, tooltip-font-size, tooltip-padding, tooltip-radius, tooltip-shadow token mappings.
4) Component API: props for density ("regular"|"compact"), helper (string), meta (string), tooltip (string | null), tooltipTriggerPosition ("inline"|"end").
5) Design spec includes visual examples with long helpers, zero-height containers, mobile width breakpoints, and localized examples (DE/JP) to validate wrapping.
6) Accessibility: screen reader reads helper text when field receives focus; when validation error appears it is moved to role="alert" for immediate announcement.

Implementation notes / trade-offs:
- Reserve space versus allow shift: we default to reserving a two-line height to avoid jumps for most forms; in extremely constrained UIs we allow opt-out (prop: reserveSpace=false) for maximum density at risk of jumps.
- Tooltip vs inline helper: tooltips are for non-critical advanced guidance and should be used sparingly; errors and required guidance should remain inline to ensure discoverability.
- Motion: only use subtle crossfade (50ms) for helper content changes; avoid position motion to reduce cognitive load in dense forms.

Links:
- Figma frames: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/forms-helper-stack (prototype folder)
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Adaptive+Helper+Stack
- Example implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/8402

Notes for engineering:
- Expose tokens in the CSS variables namespace: --rw-helper-font-size, --rw-helper-gap, --rw-helper-line-height, --rw-helper-color-regular, --rw-helper-color-compact.
- Provide a small JS utility to calculate reservedHeight based on density and whether meta is present to keep logic consistent across platforms.
- Add visual regression tests for: dense-form-no-helper, dense-form-with-helper, dense-form-with-helper+meta, tooltip-open, tooltip-closing-with-escape, long-helper-wrapping.

Risks:
- Backward compatibility: existing apps that depended on auto-shrinking layouts may see layout regressions; we'll include migration notes and an opt-out flag.
- Localization: long languages could require slightly larger reserved height; include a localized buffer token and validate in QA.

Next steps:
- Run 1-week guerrilla usability sessions with 4 product teams to validate discoverability of tooltip vs inline helper.
- Finalize tokens and hand off code-ready specs to ENG by 2026-03-19.
